sections.content: You know *por un lado* from B1 Unit 23, *mientras que* from B1 Unit 12 and *sin embargo* from A2 Unit 28. *Por una parte … por otra* is the same pair in a slightly more written form: the first half announces that a second half is coming, and the second half usually brings the contrasting point. Either half can be *por otra*, *por otra parte* or *por otro lado*. *Mientras que* ("whereas") sets two facts side by side inside one sentence, without a judgement. It is not *mientras* ("while") from A2 Unit 13: the extra *que* gives it the sense of contrast.

sections.title: Two sides of a point
rows: Por una parte, el curso es interesante; por otra, es muy caro.
On the one hand, the course is interesting; on the other, it is very expensive.
Por una parte, trabajo menos; por otro lado, gano menos.
On the one hand, I work less; on the other, I earn less.
Mis padres prefieren el campo, mientras que yo prefiero la ciudad.
My parents prefer the countryside, whereas I prefer the city.
En el campo hay silencio; en cambio, en la ciudad hay mucha vida.
In the countryside there is silence; in the city, by contrast, there is a lot of life.

sections.content: Do not open with *por una parte* and then forget the second half: the listener is waiting for it. *Mientras que* needs two different subjects or situations that you compare; the verb after it is an ordinary indicative verb.
